title: Symmetry introduction
examples: How do I check if something is symmetrical?
Can you show me a mirror line?

explain.say: Symmetry means both sides match. Look at a butterfly. Its two wings match.
You can check with a fold. Fold a paper shape in half. Open it and look at the fold line.
If the two halves match, the shape has symmetry. The fold line is the line of symmetry.
You can also use a mirror. Stand it on the line. The mirror shows the other half.
A heart has one line of symmetry. It goes straight down the middle.

draw.text: Heart: 1 line of symmetry, down the middle

faq.q: What is a line of symmetry?
faq.a: A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves. If you fold the shape on this line, both sides match up.
asks: Where is the line of symmetry?

faq.q: How do I use the folding test?
faq.a: Fold the shape on the line you think is the line of symmetry. If the edges line up exactly, it has symmetry.
asks: Can I fold it to check?
What does the folding test show?

faq.a: Yes, a heart shape usually has one line of symmetry going straight down the middle. The left side mirrors the right side.
No, not every shape has symmetry. A shape must be perfectly balanced on both sides to have a line of symmetry.
asks: What if it is not symmetrical?

faq.q: What is the difference between a mirror line and a line of symmetry?
faq.a: They are the same thing in maths. Both lines split a shape into two matching halves. The mirror just helps you see it.
asks: What is the other name for this line?

facts: Symmetry means that one side matches the other side.
The folding test helps us find the line of symmetry.
A line of symmetry is always a straight line.
A butterfly shape has one line of symmetry, down the middle.

quiz.say: Look at the letters. Tap the letter with a line of symmetry.
quiz.why: Fold A down the middle. The two halves match.

wrong.0: Fold F down the middle, and the two halves look different.
wrong.2: Fold J down the middle, and the two halves look different.

quiz.say: Fold a paper heart down the middle. Tap what you see.
quiz.why: A heart has a line of symmetry down the middle. Its two halves match.

wrong.1: Both sides of a heart are the same size, so the halves match.
wrong.2: Each half of a heart is the same shape, so the halves match.

quiz.say: Think about a line of symmetry. Tap what it does.
quiz.why: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match. Each half is a mirror image of the other.

wrong.0: A line along the top edge leaves the whole shape on one side.
wrong.1: The line can be any length, as long as the two halves match.
